capitals.name: Arles
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Arles'. The page gives no change of seat; Conrad the Peaceful was buried at Vienne (Conrad the Peaceful page). From 1032 the kings were the emperors.

rulers.name: Rudolph II
rulers.note: King of Upper Burgundy from 912, ruler of the united kingdom from 933 (Rudolph II page); died 12 or 13 July 937.

rulers.name: Conrad the Peaceful
rulers.note: Otto I held the regency during his minority; died 19 October 993 and was buried at Saint-Andre-le-Bas, Vienne.

rulers.name: Rudolph III
rulers.note: Reign 19 October 993 to 6 September 1032; died without legitimate issue.

rulers.name: Conrad II (Holy Roman Emperor)
rulers.note: King of Burgundy from 6 September 1032 (infobox) to 4 June 1039; crowned at Payerne on 2 February 1033. The later kings are the emperors; the pages opened give no list for them.

correction.text: the united Kingdom of Upper and Lower Burgundy as Cliopatria draws it from 936

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 933-935: Cliopatria begins the row in 936, but 'In 933, king Hugh of Italy ceded Lower Burgundy to king Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy' and the realm 'was established in 933 by the unification of Lower Burgundy with the Upper Burgundy' (Kingdom of Arles page; Rudolph II page agrees). The land is the 936 shape. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Lower Burgundy (900-935) overlaps it by 294 cells for 933-935; the eu-07 dossier should close that row's Burgundian share in 933.

117,221 km2 for 936-959. The page puts the kingdom 'from the Mediterranean in the south to the High Rhine in the north, and from the Western Alps in the east to the Rhone basin in the west', roughly south-east France, Franche-Comte, Romandy and the Aosta Valley. Measured on the gazetteer grid the shape covers 365 of the 381 cells of the region 'Kingdom of Burgundy (Arles)': Provence 117/121, Dauphine 82/82, Savoy 46/46, Franche-Comte 62/66, Valais 21/21, Aosta 13/13, and 94 of the 167 cells of Switzerland (the German-speaking east is rightly outside). The page gives no area, so there is no infobox comparison. The strip from Basel to Zurich (17 cells) came from Germany in 926 (kingdom-of-germany ledger).
117,176 km2 in the single year 960: the same land as 936 (a handful of cells differ). 937 Conrad the Peaceful succeeds under Otto I's regency (Conrad the Peaceful page); no territorial change.
117,013 km2 for 961-989: the same land. Provence page: 'Named marquis in 975, William made Arles his capital' (the marquisate of Provence, inside the kingdom); no change of border.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 990 shape unchanged, valid for 990-1005 only; from 1006 the next keyframe applies

keyframe_review.note: 116,942 km2 for 990-1009. Conrad the Peaceful 'died on 19 October 993' and Rudolph III succeeded (Conrad the Peaceful and Rudolph III pages). 'Rudolph in 1006 ceded the city of Basel to his nephew Henry II' (Rudolph III page), so the shape holds for 990-1005 only; Basel leaves in the next keyframe. keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1006-1009: the 990 shape without the city of Basel, which Rudolph III ceded to Henry II in 1006 (Rudolph III page). About 3 cells.

correction.text: the 1033 extent of the kingdom without Basel

keyframe_review.note: 117,029 km2 for 1010-1033, less Basel (ceded 1006). Dated events on the page: 1011 Rudolph gives Ermengarde the County of Vienne and Sermorens (internal); in 1016 Henry II 'succeeded in negotiating Rudolph to name him as his successor' at Strasbourg and the Burgundian nobles 'quickly submitted' to him against Otto-William, confirmed by a diet at Mainz in 1018; Conrad II 'occupied Basel' after 1024; 'Rudolph died in 1032' without legitimate issue. These move no border; they make the kingdom an Empire-bound heir state from 1016.

correction.text: the kingdom as an imperial kingdom: its 1033 extent without Basel, valid 1034-1039

keyframe_review.note: 18,280 km2: a strip in Cote-d'Or and Saone-et-Loire (bbox 3.60-5.59 E, 46.09-47.99 N), not one cell of which lies inside the 1033 Arles shape. It lies wholly inside Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy shapes (76 of 76 cells in 1010 and in 1385; the duchy's own row skips 1018-1384) and 75 of 76 cells inside the Upper Burgundy row of 950; it is not the Kingdom of Arles, which the page puts 'from the Mediterranean in the south to the High Rhine in the north' and in the 'Rhone basin'. After 6 September 1032 the kingdom 'was incorporated into the Holy Roman Empire, though its territories operated with considerable autonomy' (Kingdom of Arles page); Conrad II was crowned king of Burgundy at Payerne on 2 February 1033 and 'officially incorporated Burgundy into the Holy Roman Empire' at Geneva on 1 August 1034 (Conrad II page). The correction keeps the kingdom's 1033 extent. Cliopatria's Holy Roman Empire shape covers 482 of its 484 cells for 1034-1259, so the renderer should show Arles as an imperial kingdom inside the Empire (a lighter tint or an association), not a second colour on the same cells. The Burgundy strip belongs to the eu-10 Duchy of Burgundy dossier.

region.text: Upper and Lower Burgundy united: Provence and the Rhone valley, Dauphine, Savoy, Franche-Comte, western Switzerland and the Aosta Valley

ledger.note: 933: Rudolph II unites Upper and Lower Burgundy into one kingdom. The kingdom 'was a realm established in 933 by the unification of Lower Burgundy with the Upper Burgundy' (Kingdom of Arles page); the Conrad the Peaceful page calls Rudolph II 'the first ruler over the united kingdom of Upper and Lower Burgundy since 933'.

region.text: Lower Burgundy, Provence and the lower Rhone, the part of Hugh's Cliopatria shape inside the Arles shape

ledger.note: 933: Hugh of Italy cedes Lower Burgundy to Rudolph II. 'In 933, Rudolph II acquired the Kingdom of Lower Burgundy' from Hugh, 'in exchange for the waiver of his claims to the Italian crown' (Rudolph II page); 'king Hugh of Italy ceded Lower Burgundy to king Rudolph II of Upper Burgundy' (Kingdom of Arles page). Cliopatria keeps its Lower Burgundy row to 935.
1006: Rudolph III cedes Basel to Henry II. 'Rudolph in 1006 ceded the city of Basel to his nephew Henry II', who had been elected king of Germany in 1002 (Rudolph III page).

1032: Rudolph III dies without heirs and the kingdom passes to the Salian emperor Conrad II. 'Rudolph III died without issue; kingdom inherited by Emperor Conrad II: 6 September 1032' (Kingdom of Arles page); Conrad was crowned at Payerne on 2 February 1033, defeated Odo II of Blois in the summer campaigns of 1033 and 1034 and incorporated Burgundy into the Empire at Geneva on 1 August 1034 (Conrad II page). Under the 1006 treaty the kingdom passed to Conrad II (Kingdom of Arles page); Henry II's succession right had been confirmed at a diet in Mainz in 1018 (Rudolph III page).

1246: Provence passes to Charles of Anjou. The Provence infobox gives 'Passage at the Maison d'Anjou: 1246' and the body says Provence was 'a fiefdom of the Holy Roman Empire, which it remained until 1246', but the same infobox has 'Holy Roman Empire (1032-1481)' (reviewer eu-08-a: confidence lowered to 2 for that contradiction); 'In 1246, the French prince Charles I of Anjou succeeded in acquiring the County of Provence' (Kingdom of Arles page). The county remained in the kingdom in law.

region.text: the Vivarais, west of the Rhone

ledger.note: 1306: the Vivarais is recognised as French. 'this annexation occurred gradually during the 13th century and was formally recognized in 1306' (Kingdom of Arles page). The year is the page's; the Vivarais is named from the Ardeche by the researcher.
1312: Lyon passes to the French crown. The Lyonnais was 'formalized in a 1312 treaty between Archbishop Peter of Savoy and Philip IV of France' (Kingdom of Arles page).

1349: the Dauphine is sold to the French crown. 'In 1349, the Dauphine was transferred from the last non-royal Dauphin' to the future Charles V, who became Dauphin; Humbert II's 'sale of his lordship to King Philip VI in 1349' (Dauphine page). The Dauphine remained a formal imperial fief and Charles was made imperial vicar in 1378 (Kingdom of Arles page).

1361: Charles IV transfers Savoy from the Kingdom of Burgundy to the Kingdom of Germany. 'In 1361, Emperor Charles IV transferred the County of Savoy from the Kingdom of Burgundy' (Savoy page; the Kingdom of Arles page says it 'formally remained until 1797').

region.text: what was left of the nominal kingdom in 1384: Franche-Comte, western Switzerland, Aosta and the rest not yet French

ledger.note: 1384: the kingdom is a name only. The page gives no single end date: 'Disestablished: 15th century', 'since the 14th century the imperial rule over the kingdom became mainly nominal', the last dated act is the grant of the vicariate to the Dauphin Charles on 7 January 1378, and the title lasted to 1806. 1384 is Cliopatria's last year for the row, used here as a bridge.

wars.name: Rudolph III and Count Otto-William
wars.outcome: In 1016 Rudolph III fell out with Count Otto-William over the investiture of the archbishop of Besancon; at Strasbourg Rudolph named Henry II his successor, Henry marched against Otto-William and the Burgundian nobles quickly submitted; a diet at Mainz in 1018 confirmed Henry's succession right.
wars.note: No land changed hands; it made the kingdom Henry's and then Conrad II's inheritance.

wars.name: Odo II of Blois's invasion of Burgundy
wars.outcome: 'In 1032, he invaded the Kingdom of Burgundy on the death of Rudolph III' (Odo II page); 'In two large-scale military summer campaigns in 1033 and 1034, Conrad defeated Odo' and on 1 August 1034 incorporated Burgundy into the Empire; the Burgundian and Provencal nobles paid homage at Zurich in 1034 (Conrad II page).
wars.note: The pages name no district Odo held, so no zone is drawn and no contest is entered in the ledger. Odo died on 15 November 1037 at Bar-le-Duc after invading Lorraine.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes the kingdom's frontier; the 1006 cession of Basel and the 1312 treaty for Lyon are the only dated boundary acts and are sharp only at those places. After 1032 the kingdom is nominal and its lands belong to counts, archbishops and the Dauphin.

notes: Kingdom of Arles (Cliopatria 936..1384). PAGE BUDGET: 9 pages used (Arles, Conrad the Peaceful, Rudolph III, Odo II of Blois, Conrad II, Provence, Dauphine, Rudolph II, Savoy). The page gives no area, so no infobox comparison. STRUCTURAL FINDING (Cliopatria): 936..1033 is the real kingdom (117,000 km2: 365 of 381 cells of the gazetteer's 'Kingdom of Burgundy (Arles)'). The five rows 1034..1384 (18,000-21,000 km2) are a strip in Cote-d'Or and Saone-et-Loire with no cell in common with the 936..1033 shape: they lie wholly (76 of 76 cells) inside Cliopatria's Duchy of Burgundy shapes of 1010 and 1385 (the duchy's own rows skip 1018-1384) and 75 of 76 inside the 'Upper Burgundy' row of 950, so they are the duchy's land under the wrong Name. All eleven are marked wrong; the strip should go to the eu-10 duchy-of-burgundy dossier. The true kingdom after 1032 is an imperial kingdom: Cliopatria's Holy Roman Empire shape covers 482 of its 484 cells until 1259 and the minor-state rows (Savoy, Dauphine, Free County of Burgundy, Orange, Swiss Confederation, France) cover most of it afterwards. The new keyframes keep it as a nominal shell less the pieces that left (Basel 1006, Provence 1246, Vivarais 1306, Lyon 1312, Dauphine 1349, Savoy 1361); the renderer or orchestrator must decide whether to draw it (a lighter tint over the Empire, or an association per rule 4) or not at all; the HRE dossier (eu-08-b) should record Arles as a component. Start 933 (page) against Cliopatria 936; end 1384 is Cliopatria's last year, confidence 1: the page gives 'Disestablished: 15th century'. Not settled: (1) the districts held by Odo II of Blois 1032-1034 (no page names them; war listed with no zone); (2) Provence 1246-1481 has no Cliopatria row (a county of Provence dossier is needed; of Provence's 121 gazetteer cells only about 12 lie in the rows checked for 1260: France 7, Dauphine 3, HRE Minor States 1, Orange 1); (3) the Free County of Burgundy before 1333 (the page does not date the Hohenstaufen and later holders; 1157 Besancon diet and 1178 coronation are noted only); (4) the German-speaking Swiss lands were never in the kingdom, the shape is right; (5) Venaissin and Orange: successor table, no dates. Cliopatria's Upper Burgundy rows (upper-burgundy 887..959, upper-burgundy-and-italy 922..925) and Kingdom of Lower Burgundy (900..935) need a decision from eu-07 on whether they are this state's predecessors; the Arles page says it was 'preceded by Upper Burgundy; Lower Burgundy'.
